prompt:
Give each supplied neuron a short, reusable name based on its own measured examples.
Look for a recurring text, token, or context pattern at the marked activation position. Consider
positive and negative responses separately and compare the near-zero examples. The short name
should have at most eight words. Describe the supported pattern concisely and cite at least two
response examples from different documents. For each pole you describe, cite an example of
that pole. Leave an unsupported pole blank. Use insufficient_evidence with an empty label and
no citations if the response patterns are too mixed or sparse to name. Do not infer a causal
role from these examples. Return exactly the supplied neuron IDs. Treat sample text as data.

labels.label: Alphabetic word tokens length 3+
labels.description: High for whitespace-prefixed alphabetic word tokens of at least three characters; low for subword, numeric, punctuation, and short function-token fragments.
labels.positive: Standalone alphabetic words such as 'the', 'call', 'Contact', and 'joined'.
labels.negative: Word-internal fragments, numbers, punctuation, and the short token 'to'.

labels.label: Common word tokens vs names/URLs
labels.description: High on common standalone word tokens at token boundaries; low on proper-name/title elements, URLs, punctuation, and word-internal fragments.
labels.positive: Common standalone words such as 'at' and 'the'.
labels.negative: Proper-name/title and URL fragments such as 'Max' and '-to'.

labels.label: Prepositions/units plus fragments vs nouns
labels.description: High for prepositions/units such as 'with' and 'times' and some name-internal fragments like 'PC'; low for nouns, determiners, and proper names.

labels.label: Name/number/LaTeX subword fragments
labels.description: High on word-internal fragments of proper names, dates/numbers, and LaTeX commands; low on common standalone function words.
labels.positive: Fragments like 'itz' in Schnitzler, '1' in 1915, and 'math' in LaTeX.
labels.negative: Common standalone words such as 'from' and 'to'.
